plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float on feathery, thread-fine foliage. They sway above garden beds and meadows, and bees and butterflies visit them constantly. In mild autumns the flowers keep coming until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to first frost in the Northern Hemisphere. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms from spring into summer, so October is a peak month.
plants.location: Gardens worldwide. The species is native to Mexico and is widely naturalized across the Americas.
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony. It was chosen for the flowers' neatly arranged, symmetrical petals.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus
plants.description: Dense, bottle-brush-shaped spikes of bright red stamens cover the branch tips. They draw nectar-feeding birds such as honeyeaters and lorikeets. In Australia the shrub puts on a spectacular show through spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in Australia (September to December), with scattered repeat flowering
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including New South Wales and Queensland, and gardens in mild climates worldwide
plants.funFact: The red 'brush' is made of stamens, not petals. The actual petals are tiny and fall away quickly.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink flowers push straight out of the bare ground in autumn, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and woodland edges. The strap-like leaves appear the following spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, typically September to October in Europe
plants.location: Damp meadows and open woods across central and western Europe, including Britain, Germany and France
plants.funFact: It isn't a true crocus. It is a member of the lily family and contains colchicine, a toxic compound that is also used in plant breeding and medicine.
